segmenti.tekst: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ نَحْمَدُهُ وَنَسْتَعِينُهُ وَنَسْتَغْفِرُهُ
segmenti.prevod: All praise belongs to Allah; we praise Him, seek His help and ask His forgiveness.

segmenti.tekst: وَنَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ مِنْ شُرُورِ أَنْفُسِنَا وَمِنْ سَيِّئَاتِ أَعْمَالِنَا مَنْ يَهْدِهِ اللَّهُ فَلَا مُضِلَّ لَهُ، وَمَنْ يُضْلِلْ فَلَا هَادِيَ لَهُ
segmenti.prevod: We seek refuge in Allah from the evils of our souls and from our bad deeds. Whomever Allah guides, none can lead astray, and whomever He leaves astray, none can guide.

segmenti.tekst: وَأَشْهَدُ أَنْ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ وَأَشْهَدُ أَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا عَبْدُهُ وَرَسُولُهُ
segmenti.prevod: I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, Who has no partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and messenger.

segmenti.tekst: أَرْسَلَهُ اللَّهُ بِالْحَقِّ بَشِيرًا وَنَذِيرًا وَسِرَاجًا مُنِيرًا لِيُنْذِرَ مَنْ كَانَ حَيًّا وَيَحِقَّ الْقَوْلُ عَلَى الْكَافِرِينَ صَلَّى اللَّهُ تَعَالَى عَلَيْهِ وَعَلَى آلِهِ الطَّيِّبِينَ الطَّاهِرِينَ وَأَصْحَابِهِ الْكِرَامِ الْهُدَاةِ الْمُهْتَدِينَ وَسَلَّمَ تَسْلِيمًا كَثِيرًا إِلَى يَوْمِ الدِّينِ
segmenti.prevod: Allah sent him with the truth as a bearer of glad tidings, a warner and a light-giving lamp, to warn whoever is alive (of heart) and so that the Word may be fulfilled against the disbelievers (Ya-Sin 36:70). May Allah the Exalted bless him and his good and pure family and his noble companions, the rightly guided who guided others, and grant him abundant peace until the Day of Judgement.

segmenti.tekst: قَالَ اللَّهُ فِي كِتَابِهِ الْكَرِيمِ يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ حَقَّ تُقَاتِهِ وَلَا تَمُوتُنَّ إِلَّا وَأَنْتُمْ مُسْلِمُونَ أَمَّا بَعْدُ
segmenti.prevod: Allah says in His noble Book: “O you who believe, fear Allah as He deserves to be feared, and do not die except as Muslims.” (Al Imran 3:102). To proceed:

segmenti.tekst: Praise belongs to Allah alone, the Exalted, subhanahu wa ta'ala, the Lord of all the worlds, the Lord of the Day of Judgement, the Lord of jinn and mankind. May blessings and peace be upon His Messenger, the beloved Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam (peace be upon him),

upon his family, upon his companions, and upon all those who follow the path, the path of the Qur'an, the path of the Sunnah of Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam. Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says in the Qur'an… [unclear] to Adam, alayhis-salam (peace be upon him): "وَقُلْنَا يَا آدَمُ اسْكُنْ أَنْتَ وَزَوْجُكَ الْجَنَّةَ وَكُلَا مِنْهَا رَغَدًا حَيْثُ شِئْتُمَا وَلَا تَقْرَبَا هَٰذِهِ الشَّجَرَةَ فَتَكُونَا مِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ" He says: "O Adam, dwell in Jannah (Paradise), you and your wife,

and stay in it and eat from wherever you wish of the fruits of Jannah, but do not under any circumstances approach this tree, this tree, lest you be among the wrongdoers, those who have wronged themselves." "فَأَزَلَّهُمَا الشَّيْطَانُ عَنْهَا فَأَخْرَجَهُمَا مِمَّا كَانَا فِيهِ" – then Shaytan deceived them, made them eat from that tree, and drove them out of Jannah for that sin, or because of that sin they had committed.

In this Qur'anic ayah, my dear brothers, Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, reminds us that man's abode, his true abode, is Jannah. That man's true abode is Jannah. And that a person should long to return to his true home. Because our true home is Jannah.
Sometimes a person is forced to leave his hearth, his home, just as Adam, alayhis-salam, was forced, because of the sin he committed, to leave Jannah.

So too our people, when they go abroad – you know that in the 1960s our people went in great numbers to Turkey. And today they are emigrating in great numbers across Europe, but that desire, that love for their homeland always remains, so most people go abroad with the intention or the aim of earning money, coming back, building a house, starting a family, and so on and so forth.

And in the same way a person should long for Jannah. Because Jannah is our home – not Jahannam (Hellfire), not this world. Not Jahannam, not this world, but Jannah, my dear brothers. Jannah is our true home, our true abode.

But we have stopped longing for Jannah. This world has deceived us. And Allah warns us about this world. What does Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, say in the Qur'an? And do not, He says, let the life of this world deceive you. This world, dear brothers, is only a stop along the way. This world is only a stop along the way. What does the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, say?

He says: "Kullu ummati yadkhulunal-jannata illa man aba" – he says: "All people, that is, of my ummah, will enter Jannah, except the one who refuses to enter Jannah." The companions were astonished and said: "How, O Messenger, man aba?" They said: "How, who would refuse to enter Jannah? Who is that?" The Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, said: "Man ata'ani dakhalal-jannata" – whoever obeys me will enter Jannah – "wa man 'asani faqad aba" – and whoever disobeys me, he says, he refuses, refuses to enter, refuses to enter Jannah.

Through His Messenger Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, Allah promises us Jannah for small deeds, for minor deeds, believe me, deeds that are not great, that are not difficult. He promises us Jannah if we do them. The Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, says: "Allah has 99 beautiful names; whoever applies them in his life, acts according to them, will enter Jannah." Here is one way: how a person applies Allah's names in his life, how he lives by them.
In the last hutba (Friday sermon) we spoke about Allah's mercy. One of Allah's names is Ar-Rahman, the Merciful. What does the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, say?
الرَّاحِمُونَ يَرْحَمُهُمُ الرَّحْمَٰنُ
segmenti.prevod: “The merciful are shown mercy by the Most Merciful.” (hadith, Abu Dawud and at-Tirmidhi)

segmenti.tekst: "Those who are merciful, Allah will have mercy on them." So it is up to a person to be merciful. It is up to a person to have a good opinion of Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala. Not to think that Allah will do him harm, not to think that Allah hates him, but that He is merciful, that our Lord is merciful.

Also, among Allah's names is Al-Basir, the One who sees everything, the One who sees everything. So when a person wants to commit some sin, something that is haram, he should be aware that Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, sees him; he should behave among people, that is, he should behave when he is alone the way he behaves among people,

with good character, with respect, knowing that Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, sees him. So when he works in some place where he could embezzle someone else's money, take someone else's money, let him remember that Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, sees him, and say: "I will not do that.
I will not do that – not because of people, whether someone will catch me or not, but because Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, sees me." When someone invites him to a gambling house: "No, I won't.
Not because people would see me or not see me… but because it is haram. I will not earn haram money."

When a person wants to backbite someone, he must know that among Allah's names is As-Sami', the One who hears everything. So when he wants to backbite or curse someone – you know, it often happens that a person talks with someone and, as soon as the other turns his back, he curses him: "That so-and-so," he says, "this and that" – he must know that Allah is the One who hears everything. So if he applies these names of Allah, lives by them, [unclear], Allah

promises him, promises him Jannah. The second thing for which Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, promises Jannah is reciting Ayat al-Kursi, or, as we call it, the tesbih-dova. If a person recites the tesbih-dova after the prayer, nothing separates him from Jannah except death. It is the greatest ayah in the Qur'an. Why? Because at the beginning of this ayah Allah praises Himself. Allah praises Himself,

and says that there is no deity worthy of worship except Him, that He is the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining, that everything in the heavens and on the Earth is His. A person should, dear brothers, take a little time to read these meanings. As believers we must know, we must know what Ayat al-Kursi is, what it means, what Al-Fatihah means, what Qul huwallahu ahad means, Allahumma Rabbana. He says: "I don't have time." How do you not have time? He knows the biography of the players, of all

the footballers: when he was born, where he moved, where the transfer was, to which league, how many millions – he knows everything. But when it comes time, dear brothers, to know something about the faith, Allah's religion, he says: "I don't have time." He has no time. He says: "I don't have time, I'm looking after my parents." By Allah, he has no time, he says, to come to the mosque, [unclear] parents – he is not in the mosque. These are only excuses, dear brothers, these are only excuses. Excuses until the angel of death comes.
The next thing for which Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, promises Jannah is, he says: whoever raises two daughters in Islam and treats them well, Allah promises him Jannah.
[unclear], dear brothers, how Islam has elevated women! What these Western media feed us is a story for little children. In the West, woman is used as a commodity.

What is a naked woman doing next to a car, why should a naked woman be commenting on or presenting the weather forecast, and so on? So she is used as a commodity, to attract people's gazes, or to that merchandise being sold.

But Islam has elevated women. Whoever wants to know what rights Islam has given women, let him inform himself a little better and read, so that he sees how Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, has elevated women in Islam.

You know what the Arabs used to do before Islam came. They buried the dead, that is, they buried their daughters alive. A companion narrates, after he had accepted Islam: "I took my daughter into the valleys of Mecca, and I dug a hole.

And she was alive, already grown, three or four years old. And I," he says, "started to bury her. And she," he says, "was wiping the dust from my face." And believe me, those people were worse than animals.
A lioness, a wild beast, will not kill its child, that is, its cub, in such a way. And Allah elevated, elevated her in Islam. And all of us who have daughters know what a blessing that is.
What a blessing it is! It is told that a man, that is, when he married, very much wanted to have sons. But his first child was – what? A daughter. It was night, so he named her Layla – night.
And he would always, it is said, call her, call out to her: "Layla, [unclear]… my black night." After her he had many sons. The time came and he reached old age. [unclear].

His sons abandoned him and left. Then a woman came who took care of him. He asked her: "Who are you?" What does she say? She says: "Ana laylatukas-sawda'" – she says: "I am your black night," that is: "I am that daughter of yours.

I am that daughter of yours." His sons abandoned him and left; the daughter stayed. And believe me, a daughter, not just sometimes but in most cases, is a greater blessing than sons, my dear brothers. That is why Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, promises this reward.

The next thing for which Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, through His Messenger, promises us Jannah is, he says: whoever prays the Fajr prayer and the Asr prayer, especially in congregation, especially in congregation, Allah promises him Jannah.

Why Fajr? Because it is hard for the munafiqun (hypocrites). Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says: and when they stand up for prayer, they stand up lazily, dragging themselves, so that people would see them – that is the only purpose [unclear]. And He says: whoever prays the prayer will be, He says, the whole day under Allah's… Why?

A person sets his alarm clock for seven o'clock to go to work, yet he will not pray the Fajr prayer, while he fears his boss. What does Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, say: "Wa takhshan-nasa wallahu ahaqqu an takhshahu" – He says: and you fear people, while Allah has more right that you fear Him. And Allah has more right that we fear Him. What will we do when the angel of death comes to us? There will be no boss, no [unclear], no family. That is why a person should reflect. And likewise Asr.

The Asr prayer is a special prayer, because that is when people are returning from work. Most people [unclear], neglect Asr. Those who pray here with us – how few people there are at Asr. It is few, very few. What does Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, say in the

Qur'an? "Guard the prayers, especially the middle prayer" – and that is the Asr prayer. The Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, says: "Whoever abandons the Asr prayer, his deeds will be nullified." Now the scholars say: his deeds for that day will be nullified, all the deeds he did will be nullified, and so on. That is why Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, promises a reward, and that is Jannah. And the last thing we will mention today is seeking Islamic knowledge. The Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, says:
"Whoever follows a path in seeking knowledge, Allah will make easy for him a path to Jannah."
Why? Because with that knowledge he will know how to walk the path that leads, that leads to Jannah.

Believe me, dear brothers, many of us do not know how to perform wudu (ablution) correctly, how to pray correctly, how to make up missed prayers. And a believer should know all of this. And all under the excuse: "I don't have time." I tell him: believe me, we have people here who come to the study circles of Qur'an tafsir and Qur'an memorisation – when you shake hands with them, it is as if you are shaking hands with a stone.
Their hands are that hard from work, from heavy work. But that did not stop them from coming to learn the Arabic letters, to learn the basics of the faith.

Instead of a person using the time between Maghrib and Isha to learn something, to read something, to sit down… We all have phones now, and it is very easy to get this information. To sit in the mosque, at home – no, we look for how and where we will drink coffee, with whom we will drink coffee.

He says: "I don't have time" – what kind of… – especially in places where people smoke, where they backbite, and so on and so on and so forth. So that prayer has had no effect on us. That is why a person should learn the basics of his faith, so that he can worship Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, in the correct way.
Why does the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, mention to us these things by which we can enter Jannah? To motivate us to do good, to do good deeds, towards goodness.

And that is the goal of Islam, to direct us towards goodness, to direct us towards Jannah. I ask Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, to forgive our sins and the sins of our parents. I ask Him, the Exalted, to admit us into Jannah.
آمِينَ يَا رَبَّ الْعَالَمِينَ أَقُولُ قَوْلِي هَٰذَا وَأَسْتَغْفِرُ اللَّهَ لِي وَلَكُمْ فَاسْتَغْفِرُوهُ إِنَّهُ هُوَ الْغَفُورُ الرَّحِيمُ
segmenti.prevod: Amen, O Lord of the worlds. I say these words of mine and ask Allah for forgiveness for myself and for you, so ask Him for forgiveness; truly He is the Oft-Forgiving, the Most Merciful.
